L17@P1: by S. LOJASIEWICZ (Krak6w)
L18@P1: The triangulability question for algebraic sets was first considered by van de Waerden [15] in 1929, and for analytic sets by Lefschetz [5], Koop- man and Brown [4], and Lefschetz and Whitehead [6], in 1930-1933. In fact,
L19@P1: j5] and [6] deal with triangulation of « analytical complex » (which is a finite disjoint collection with compact union of subsets of 1R~ each being an
L20@P1: open and relatively compact subset of an analytic subset of an open set in
L21@P1: A lack of a convenient technique at that time was probably the reason
L22@P1: for the proofs being rather sketched. Therefore, according to an opinion of
L23@P1: many mathematiciens, it is of some interest to give a new detailed proof.
L24@P1: This is just the purpose of the present paper, and actually we give a somewhat more general result: simultaneous triangulation of any locally finite
L25@P1: collection of semi analytic subsets of 1Rn or, owing to the Grauert imbedding
L26@P1: theorem [3], of any countable real analytic manifold. Moreover, our formulation of the result is somewhat more precise; it follows e.g. that in any
L27@P1: exemple of Milnor’s type [9] the homeomorphism between the polyhedra has to
L28@P1: have a singularity of non-algebraic type (it can not have the property (A)
L29@P1: (see § 3)). However the frame of idea of the construction we give is that of
L30@P1: Lefschetz ([5] and [6]).
L31@P1: The semi-analytic (resp. semi-algebraic) sets are those which can be locally given by analytic (resp. algebraic) inequalities (see [13], [14] and [8]).
L32@P1: We may observe that the body of an « analytic complex » is exactly the
L33@P1: same as a compact semi-analytic set. We will need certain basic properties
L34@P1: of semi-aualytic sets ; 3these are only stated in § 1, and will be contained
L35@P1: with proofs in papers to appear separately.
L36@P1: The method we use is that of normal decompositions of semi-analytic
L37@P1: sets ; it follows an old idea of Osgood [10] (see also [11]), and was applied
L38@P1-2: Pervenuto alla Redazione il 18 Maggio 1964.450
L39@P2: by the author in [7] (1). The normal decompositions are certain special local
L40@P2: stratifications in the sens of Thom [14]. For the semi algebraic case an elegant Whitney’s stratification [17] can be also used.
L41@P2: The result was communicated on the Congress in Stockholm, 1962, and
L42@P2: the construction was presented in details on a seminar at the Istituto Matematico Leonida Tonelli of the University in Pisa, spring, 1963.
L43@P2: Afther having written the manuscript the autor observed that had just
L44@P2: appeared a thesis of B. Giesecke [2] concerning also the triangulation of
L45@P2: semi-analytic sets; because of the differences which seem to exist in results
L46@P2: and methods used, our article may be however of independent interest.
L47@P2: One should also mention a paper of K. Sato [19] on local triangulation
L48@P2: of real analytic varieties.
